title: Unified attribution fabric for per-route/model/customer with streaming reconciliation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a resilient, low-latency service that computes cost and latency breakdowns per-route, per-model, and per-customer, combining streaming runtime telemetry with batched billing signals. The system should support: 1) real-time leaderboards for Console dashboards (1s-5s freshness), 2) accurate daily reconciled ledgers for billing and chargeback, 3) explainability traces that tie tokens/requests to kernel/runtime shards and model variants.

Scope: Implement a microservice (Attribution Fabric) that consumes runtime spans, kernel cost estimates, batching decisions, token counts, and billing tags; runs streaming attribution to attribute each request/token across route/model/customer dimensions; and emits both rolling aggregates and reconciled daily slices. The service must integrate with: telemetry kafka topics (runtime-spans, kernel-metrics, batch-events), billing event S3 dumps, and the Console metrics store (internal-timeseries).

Design highlights: - Two-path pipeline: a streaming fast-path for near-real-time aggregates (windowed keyed tumbling/upserts) and a backfill/reconciler that corrects drift using authoritative billing slices. - Causal-span reconciliation: use request-id + causal-spans to attribute amortized GPU time and cross-request batching credits deterministically. - Deterministic assignment rules to avoid double-counting when kernels split across GPUs or when multi-tenant batches include mixed customers. - Schema: flattened attribution key (customer_id|route_id|model_hash|variant|region), time_bucket (1m/1h/day), cost_tokens, cost_gpu_ms, latency_ms_p50|p95, token_count, sample_traces.

API/Outputs: - Streaming topic: attribution-quick-agg (1m windows) for Console dashboards. - Daily ledger: attribution-daily-slices (parquet) for billing reconciliation. - Explain endpoint: /v1/attribution/explain?req_id= that returns a sampled trace and the attribution breakdown for a request (used by SRE and support).

SLOs and correctness: Near-real-time aggregates must be available <=5s after event arrival 99th percentile; daily reconciled ledgers must converge to authoritative billing within 0.1% total cost variance. Emphasize deterministic reconciliation and idempotency to avoid charging/invoice drift.

Operational runbook: autoscale streaming consumers by partition lag, circuit-break to replay consumer when upstream schema drift detected, fallback to conservative attribution (model-level only) when kernel cost signals are missing.

Trade-offs considered: - Heavy-weight per-token attribution improves explainability but increases state cardinality; we use tiered retention (full detail for 7 days, aggregated keys for 90 days). - Reconciliation complexity vs latency: opted for a fast approximate streaming path + periodic authoritative backfill to keep Console responsive while ensuring billing correctness.

Open questions: - Do we store sampled per-request traces in the same cluster as aggregates or a separate cold-store? (current opt: cold-store in long-term S3 to reduce hot-state size). - Customer tagging edge cases where customers share routes (solution: require route->owner mapping, fall back to route-level attribution with manual override).
